approach: Extend the gate's attribution walk with a mode (incremental or full replay). Incremental reads the newest checkpoint record (checkpoints/<id>.json) and judges only first-parent main commits after its main_sha, counting only intent/landing records added since its records_sha. It falls back to a full replay, with the reason reported, when the checkpoint's check version differs, its main_sha is off main, or its records_sha is not an ancestor of the records tip. Full replay ignores checkpoints for trust, judges everything, then compares with the newest checkpoint and reports a CheckpointDisagrees finding naming the checkpoint when any commit at or before its main_sha has a finding or the checkpoint cannot be located. Every report carries seconds, commits judged and records judged, in text and JSON. A gate function writes a checkpoint only after a pass. The CLI calls it unless --read-only is given or the CI environment variable is set, and after a landing. CI passes --read-only: incremental on push, --full-replay on schedule. Timings come from an ignored fixture test with about 200 landings; the printed numbers go into the CHANGELOG labeled measured-on-fixture.

decisions.choice: The checkpoint names the last passing main commit before the first pending commit; written only when the report has no findings.
decisions.reason: A pending commit's 15-minute window can still expire into a finding; a checkpoint past it would hide that finding from later incremental runs.

rejected.option: Checkpoint at the main tip even with pending commits
rejected.why: An expired pending commit would never be judged again.

decisions.choice: Incremental runs read all intents and landings for matching but count as records judged only those added since the checkpoint's records_sha (diff-tree --diff-filter=A).
decisions.reason: A new main commit may cite an older intent, so matching needs the full set; the count still reflects new work.

rejected.why: A landing for a new commit citing an older intent would be wrongly reported missing.

decisions.choice: Check version is a constant ATTRIBUTION_CHECK_VERSION in attribution.rs stored in Checkpoint.verifier_version; mismatch forces a full replay with the reason reported.
decisions.reason: Only a rule change makes past passes untrustworthy.

rejected.why: Every release would invalidate checkpoints without a rule change.

decisions.choice: Explicit --read-only flag, also implied by the CI env var; CI passes the flag and keeps permissions contents: read.
decisions.reason: Code-enforced no-write mode backed by workflow permission, per the mechanism default.

rejected.why: Not enforced in the local code path and a failed write would be noisy.

decisions.choice: Land checkpoint written from the CLI Land command after land_pr returns Landed with a merged_commit; gh.rs untouched.
decisions.reason: gh.rs is not a deliverable; the landing record is already written by land_pr first.

rejected.option: Add a checkpoint method to LandingRecords in gh.rs
rejected.why: Outside deliverables and touches fake sinks.

Re-export new API; keep legacy wrappers compiling.
CHECKPOINT_DIR constant and Checkpoint path/constructor helper; record type unchanged.
--full-replay and --read-only flags, CI-env rule, write on pass, post-landing checkpoint helper, Check doc comment.

steps: history.rs: add CHECKPOINT_DIR and path helper with a small test.
attribution.rs: add Mode, ATTRIBUTION_CHECK_VERSION, new report fields, FindingKind::CheckpointDisagrees and label.

attribution.rs: read checkpoints, pick newest, decide incremental vs forced replay (version, main_sha off main, records_sha not ancestor), start walk after checkpoint main_sha, count added records via diff-tree, time with Instant.
attribution.rs: full replay compares with newest checkpoint and adds CheckpointDisagrees; compute checkpoint_main before first pending; add write_checkpoint acting only on a clean report.
attribution.rs tests: incremental, tampered, version change, write/no-write, ignored fixture_timings.
main.rs: flags, CI-env rule, write on pass, post-landing helper with unit test, doc comment.
display.rs: text and JSON output with unit tests.
binary.rs: help, JSON and exit-code tests.
ci.yml: split attribution step by event and add --read-only.
Run cargo fmt, clippy, test; run the ignored fixture test; put printed numbers in CHANGELOG; update docs/design/records-history.md.

risks.risk: A ~200-landing fixture makes the timing test slow.
risks.mitigation: Write records in one RecordsWriter::append with many Changes; mark the test #[ignore].

risks.risk: Changing walk's signature breaks check_attribution_with_legacy and its tests.
risks.mitigation: Keep check_attribution's signature as a full-replay wrapper; add the mode function beside it.

risks.risk: A tampered checkpoint whose records_sha is not an ancestor could crash the diff.
risks.mitigation: Check ancestry first; fall back to full replay with a CheckpointDisagrees finding.
Run the ignored test, copy printed values, label measured-on-fixture.

demonstrations.method: Gate unit test: build N attributed commits, run incremental (pass writes a checkpoint), add 2 more attributed commits, run incrementally again; assert checked==2, records_judged equals new intents plus landings, mode Incremental; a FullReplay run has checked==N+2.
demonstrations.observes: Test passes: incremental judged count equals new commits and is less than the full replay's.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without checkpoint reading the incremental run judges N+2 commits and the equality assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Gate test: write a checkpoint naming an unattributed main commit with a valid records_sha; incremental passes (starts after it); FullReplay fails with Unattributed plus a CheckpointDisagrees finding whose detail contains the checkpoint id. Binary test: check --attribution --full-replay exits 2.
demonstrations.observes: Replay reports a finding naming the checkpoint and fails.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the replay trusted the checkpoint it would skip those commits, pass, and the disagreement assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: Gate test: valid checkpoint with verifier_version 'attribution/0' naming a recent commit; run incremental; assert effective mode FullReplay, replay_reason mentions version, checked equals total commit count.
demonstrations.observes: Version mismatch forces a full replay judging everything.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the version comparison only commits after the checkpoint are judged and checked is too small.

demonstrations.method: Gate and CLI tests comparing records tip before/after: (a) passing check writes one checkpoint with main sha, records tip and version; (b) failing check leaves tip unchanged; (c) --read-only and CI=true leave tip unchanged on the same repo that writes without them; (d) post-landing helper puts a checkpoint after the landing record; (e) pending commit makes the checkpoint stop before it.
demonstrations.observes: Tips move only in the writing cases.
demonstrations.fails_without: If read-only did not suppress writes the tip would move in (c); if failing runs wrote, it would move in (b).

demonstrations.method: Run lint and format checks over the whole workspace after the change; they are the gate that rejects warnings (including unused new fields/variants, needless clones) and unformatted code in the new modules and tests.
demonstrations.observes: Exits 0 with no warnings; then cargo fmt --check exits 0 with no diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any clippy warning in the new attribution, CLI or display code (e.g. an unused CheckpointDisagrees arm, needless borrow) makes clippy report it and exit non-zero under -D warnings; unformatted code makes cargo fmt --check print a diff and exit 1.

demonstrations.method: Binary test asserts help contains --full-replay, --read-only, 'incremental' and no-write wording; also read output directly.
demonstrations.observes: Help documents incremental mode, --full-replay, and that --read-only and CI never write checkpoints.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the doc comment and new args the contains assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Display unit tests assert text has 'second', 'commit(s) judged', 'record(s) judged' and JSON has numeric seconds, commits_judged, records_judged; binary test parses check --attribution --json.
demonstrations.observes: Every run reports seconds, commits and records.
demonstrations.fails_without: Assertions on summary line and JSON keys fail if fields are missing.

demonstrations.observes: Top-level permissions: contents: read unchanged; one --read-only step on push, one --read-only --full-replay step with if github.event_name == 'schedule'; no step writes or pushes a checkpoint.

demonstrations.method: Run the ignored fixture test (about 200 landings, full replay, add one landing and checkpoint, incremental one behind) and copy printed seconds into the CHANGELOG labeled measured-on-fixture, noting real-repo timing is taken after landing.
demonstrations.observes: Printed full-replay and incremental seconds match the CHANGELOG; incremental is lower and judges 1 commit.

demonstrations.method: The tamper test also asserts the full replay judged commits at or before the checkpoint and that the finding label and detail name the checkpoint id; a second test shows an unknown main_sha yields CheckpointDisagrees.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checkpoint were trusted in full replay, checked would be smaller than the total and no CheckpointDisagrees finding would appear.

open_questions: Which remote do local checkpoints get pushed to? The producer should find the remote GitLandingRecords::for_remote uses before choosing append vs append_to_remote.
Does records_branch::audit_history cost scale with the whole records history? The plan keeps it as a full audit each run.
Is a local full-replay pass allowed to write a checkpoint? The plan allows it unless read-only.
